system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
I wonder how often I'll be DMing Spotify support before they fix their app deleting my stuff.

PRECEDENTS:

[2251491] past customer: Spotify tells me to rate their app just as the app keeps bugging out...do you wanna fight, Spotify?
     spotify replied: Hey Felicia! Can you give us more info on what's happening exactly? We'd love to help

[1848931] past customer: Really disappointed with the Customer Service. No effort was made to retain a long time customer and early adopter. Clearly, this was a bad app update that corrupted the Spotify database on my phone. <link>
     spotify replied: Sorry to hear you feel that way. Check out the steps under "Downloads unexpectedly removed" at <link>

[1235792] past customer: Any news on the spotify app on the LG smart tv? I'v read you've put it down due to user unfriendly. When can i use it again?
     spotify replied: Hi! We don't have an update on this right now, but there's some more info on this at <link> 🙂

[684933] past customer: Is reputation on Spotify yet it would be really nice to use the app again
     spotify replied: Hey. Taylor Swift's 'Reputation' isn't available to stream just yet! For now, check out the singles: <link>

[2110163] past customer: Will you be updating the Spotify app for iPhone X users? It looks dumb right now.
     spotify replied: Hi! We're afraid we don't have any news about it right now. We'll be sure to let everyone know as soon as we have something to share

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
hey! sorry to hear that—can you give us more info on what's being deleted and what's happening exactly? we'd love to help

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hey Vincent! We've just replied to your DM. We'll carry on chatting there

Return the JSON scores.
text: {"correctness":4,"groundedness":5,"consistency":5,"helpfulness":4,"no_unsupported_claims":5,"rationale":"The reply appropriately asks for details and offers help in line with the precedents, though it does not acknowledge or direct the customer to continue in an existing DM conversation."}
